literal: Anger as a worthy thing having considered, he who holds [it], [his] ruin; on the ground he who struck, [his] hand will not fail [to be hurt], it is like that.
translation: The ruin of a man who holds onto anger as a worthy principle is as certain as the pain of a hand that strikes the hard ground.
modern: சினத்தை ஒரு சிறந்த பொருளாகக் கருதி மனத்துள் கொள்பவனுக்கு அழிவு நிச்சயம். அது நிலத்தில் ஓங்கி அடித்தவனின் கைக்கு வலி தப்பாததைப் போன்றது.
explanation: This couplet illustrates the inevitable self-destruction caused by holding onto anger. The word 'பொருள்' here means a thing of value or a guiding principle; treating anger as something useful is a grave mistake. Just as a person who strikes the hard ground cannot escape hurting their own hand, a person who harbors anger cannot escape their own ruin. The vivid image of striking the earth emphasizes that the damage is immediate, self-inflicted, and absolutely certain.
